tasks.title: Assassination Of A Reformed Government Official Chu Koh Ping
tasks.en:
November 29, 1938.
Morning Translation

At the time of his death he had in his possession two cents
and a pass issued by the Japanese military authorities, on
which his address was given as No.22 Teh Sing Li (德馨里),
Keshing Road.
Chu was formerly a regimental commander in the
North-western Army, but was dismissed by Marshal Feng Yu-
hsiang because of his bad reputation. After giving up
his army career, he returned to his native place at Chang-
chow where he remained until the outbreak of the Sino-
Japanese hostilities last year. After the withdrawal of
the Chinese troops from Changchow, he, together with a
number of loafers and army deserters, first oppressed the
people by levying taxes and later they surrendered to the
Japanese who organized them into a Soochow-Chengchow-Wusih
Garrison Corps of which he was appointed Chief. The Corps
is about 700 strong and well equipped. However, the
Japanese had failed to pay his men their wages of $20 each
a month as promised. About two months ago, the Corps was
disarmed and he was arrested by the Japanese as he had
refused to render assistance to the Japanese soldiers in
the campaign against guerrillas. He was taken to Soochow
and possibly through the efforts of certain persons he was
later released.
Chu came to Shanghai four days ago in company
with several others and was staying in Room No.22 of
the Liang Chi Lodging House (梁溪旅館), Hoopeh Road. He
had many acquaintances among the loafers in the western
District of Shanghai. Last night one Zung Foo-sung(陳富生)
and one Ching (金) invited him to supper, so he hurriedly
returned to the lodging house in the hope of meeting his
friends at the appointed time.
It is said that Chu had some experience of
military operations and was a good Chinese scholar. He
often wrote scrolls for others. On the day following his
arrival in Shanghai, he went to the Ta Sing tailor shop
(大新) on Foochow Road and ordered an overcoat.

Standard and other local newspapers :-

It is ascertained that the man who was murdered
yesterday at the intersection of Chekiang Road and Avenue
Edward VII was one Chu Koh-ping, age 42, native of Chang-
chow, who was formerly the Chief of the Police Defence
Corps at Wusih. He lived at No. 12 Ferry Road near the
Kawamura Memorial Tower. He used to write scrolls for
others for a living. His son-in-law, Tsu Vee-ming
(朱維明), native of Wusih, is a painter with an office
in the accountant's room of the Liang Chi Lodging House,
No.144 Hoopeh Road.
The Police are investigating the murder.
tasks.zh:
1938年11月29日。
晨间译文

他去世时身上带有两分钱和一张由日本军方当局签发的通行证，上面注明的地址为克兴路德馨里22号。
朱氏原为西北军的一名团长，但因声誉不佳被冯玉祥元帅撤职。放弃军旅生涯后，他回到家乡常州，一直居住到去年中日战事爆发。中国军队从常州撤退后，他与一群无赖和逃兵一起，起初通过征收税捐压迫百姓，后来向日本人投降，日本人将他们编组为苏常吴驻军团，并任命他为司令。该团约有700人，装备精良。然而，日本人未能按承诺每月支付其部下每人20元的薪饷。大约两个月前，该团被解除武装，他因拒绝协助日军进行反游击战行动而被日本人逮捕。他被带到苏州，可能通过某些人的努力，后来获释。
朱氏四天前与其他几人一同来到上海，住在湖北路梁溪旅馆22号房间。他在上海西区的那些无赖中有许多熟人。昨晚，陈富生（Zung Foo-sung，音译）和一位金姓人士（Ching）邀请他共进晚餐，因此他匆忙返回旅馆，希望能按时与朋友会面。
据说朱氏有一些军事作战经验，且汉学功底良好。他经常为他人书写条幅。抵达上海的第二天，他去福州路的大新裁缝店定做了一件大衣。

《标准报》及其他本地报纸：

经查实，昨日在浙江路与爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）交叉口被杀的男子名为朱国平（Chu Koh-ping），42岁，常州人，曾任无锡警察保卫团团长。他居住在河滨路川村纪念塔附近的12号。他以替人书写条幅为生。他的女婿朱维明（Tsu Vee-ming），无锡人，是一名画家，办公地点位于湖北路144号梁溪旅馆的会计室。
警方正在调查这起谋杀案。

Sir,

At 11 a.m. 31/12/33 Mr. Nee Dah Tsan (倪大椿), owner of the above filature brought to the Station a letter which was written on his behalf by a lawyer named Tsiang Pao Li (蔣保釐). 38 Avenue Edward 7th.

The letter intimated that owing to trade depression and financial difficulties the owner of the above factory was to permanently close same at about 12 noon, this date, (31/12/33) and thereby dispense with the services of the entire staff and requesting police assistance in the event of possible trouble.

On receipt of this letter uniform police and detectives were posted in the mill to take precautionary measures.

At 1.25 p.m. (31/12/33) a telephone message was received from the management to the effect that workers were creating trouble in the machine room.

A party of police with C/Inspector Foley, Inspector West and S.I. Craik immediately proceeded to the filature where numerous employees were found in the compound abusing the owner, Nee Dah Tsun. tasks.en:
Rep. 2

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.2, Special Branch No. D 5626
REPORT
Date 15 - 1 - 34

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. B. REGISTRY.
D 5626
15 - 1 - 34

Subject (in full) Discovery of communist literature at No.471 Tong Sheo Fung
(東壽坊), Range Road, on 26.1.34.
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by O.B.Ku. D.I.

With reference to the attached file on the finding of
a quantity of communist literature at No.471 Tong Sheo Fung (東壽坊)
Range Road, on 26.1.34, which was later ascertained by the
Municipal Police as being the home of a communist agent named
Bah Tung (伯 釗) who had been arrested by the Municipal Police
at 1338 Haining Road on 12.1.34 on the authority of a warrant
issued at the instance of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau.
He was extradited to the Chinese Authorities by Court order on
January 20, 1934.

Exhaustive enquiries made from the local Kuomintang
Headquarters through Supt. Tan Shao-liang finally ascertained
from Mr. Loh Yuen-fu, an officer attached to the Investigation
Department of the local Kuomintang Headquarters, that the communist
literature in question was on 5.2.34 handed over to the local
Kuomintang Authorities by order of the Second Branch of the Kiangsu
High Court for investigation and on 8.2.34 the same court sent
a notification to the local Kuomintang Authorities requesting
that the literature together with the result of findings be
transmitted to the local Public Safety Bureau to be used as
evidence in the case against Bah Tung. This request was
acceded to on March 5, 1934.

The local Kuomintang Headquarters, upon completing its
investigation, discovered that, apart from a book (two volumes)
entitled "History of Imperialist Oppression of China," which is
of an anti-Imperialist nature, the remaining literature was
purely communist propaganda.

In view of the fact that the literature has been handed
over direct to the Public Safety Bureau, it is unnecessary for
the Municipal Police to pursue this matter further.

Copy sent G. H. Kew. 15/3 '34. D. I.
Kuh Tao-hwa
Officer i/c S.B.

主题（全称） 1934年1月26日在虹口路東壽坊471号发现共产主义文献。
由 警探长 顾宝华 (Kuh Pao-hwa) 制作，由 O.B.Ku. 警探长 转呈。

关于附件中提及的于1934年1月26日在虹口路東壽坊471号发现大量共产主义文献一事，后经工部局警务处查明，该处系一名名为 Bah Tung (伯釗) 的共产党特工的住所。此人曾根据上海市公安局的请求签发的逮捕令，于1934年1月12日被工部局警务处在海宁路1338号逮捕。他于1934年1月20日经法院命令引渡给中国当局。

通过谭绍良 (Tan Shao-liang) 巡官向当地国民党总部进行的详尽查询，最终从当地国民党总部调查科官员罗元福 (Loh Yuen-fu) 先生处获悉，上述共产主义文献已于1934年2月5日奉江苏高等法院第二分院之命移交给当地国民党当局进行调查；1934年2月8日，该法院又向当地国民党当局发出通知，要求将该批文献连同调查结果一并移送当地公安局，作为起诉 Bah Tung 一案的证据。此项请求已于1934年3月5日获准执行。

当地国民党总部在完成调查后发现，除了一本（两卷本）题为《帝国主义压迫中国史》、具有反帝性质的书籍外，其余文献纯属共产主义宣传品。

鉴于该批文献已直接移交给公安局，工部局警务处无需再对此事进行进一步追究。

副本送 G. H. Kew。1934年3月15日。警探长
顾道华 (Kuh Tao-hwa)
特务科主管警官

tasks.title: Mei Foong Silk Weaving Factory - Chinese Strike Situation
tasks.en:
Koo Pai Nyiu (顧沛之)
Soochow                                D. S. Craig
Y'poo Stn.        28/2/39                     Clerk Chin Cheng Ju.

My name is Koo Pai Nyui, age 30, native of Soochow, M/cool:
employed at the Mei Fong Silk Filature, 83 Haichow Road,
residing at an unnumbered country house off Haichow Road.
    I have been employed together with Sung Ming Foo (沈明富)
and Pau Tung Kwong (包道光), residing at the same address, under
Woo Pau Jang (吳柏祥), sub-contractor, Mei Foong Silk Filature,
since July 1938 until 15th Feb. 1939 when the factory ceased work
for the Chinese New Year Festivities and has not re-opened since.
Prior to the factory closing a notice was posted by the owner
to the effect that wages would be paid on 25th Feb. 1939.
I visited my mother-in-law, named Koo Kyung Doo (顧金大)
residing 17 Toh Sing Li, Rue Du Marche, and stayed there until
the 26/2/39 on which date I returned to the factory for my
salary but Woo Pau Jang refused to pay same unless I handed
over my pass to him, this I refused to do stating that my pass
had been obtained by the proprietor of the factory. After
making this statement Woo Pau Jang again refused to pay the
wages due to me following which an argument ensued which
subsequently led to blows being struck. On the termination of the
fight which was witnessed by many other employees of the Mei
Fong Silk Filature, Woo Pau Jang stated that as a result of
the fight he had "lost face" and would therefore call several
loafers to assault and cause me bodily injury. At about 4.00 p.m.
28/2/39 a friend of mine named Pang Miau Yi (彭妙儀) informed
me that there was a crowd of loafers coming to assault me towards
(28/2/39) at the instigation of Woo Pau Jang. On receipt of this
information I went to hide at my friend Pang Miau Yi's home

Sir,

At 5.40 p.m. the 28-11-39 a telephone message was received from the management of the Mei Foong (美丰) Silk Filature, No. 83 Haichow Road, to the effect that labour trouble had broken out in the mill and that police were required to clear the premises.

A party of police headed by Inspr. Palmer immediately proceeded to the above filature and found that the workers had barricaded themselves inside and refused to open up.

After a considerable amount of parleying between detectives and workers the latter finally threw open the main gate, thus permitting the police party to enter.

The trouble, it was then ascertained, was due to the management's decision to reduce the subsistence allowance of a number of workers who had either lost their jobs or been placed on short time on account of unsatisfactory prospects in the silk manufacturing export business. These workers had refused to leave the premises unless their allowance was increased.

Fearing that if permitted to remain the operatives might sabotage the plant, Mr. Lee Loong Siau (倪能孝), managing proprietor of the concern, requested that the Police compel all employees to leave the mill premises. 由帕尔默 (Palmer) 督察率领的一队警察立即前往上述缫丝厂，发现工人们将自己 barricaded（封锁/固守）在内部，拒绝开门。

经过探员与工人之间长时间的交涉，后者最终打开了大门，从而允许警察队伍进入。

Koh Ying (郭英)
Nanking                                S.S.I. Prokofiev
W. Hongkew Stn        13-1-34                  Clerk Fang Kuo Tien

My name is Koh Ying (郭英), age 21, native of
Nanking, unemployed.    I first arrived in Shanghai from
Nanking where I studied in a middle school until the summer
of 1932, after which I lived there with my parents. I have
since been living with my cousin named Koh Miao (郭淼) at
No.63 Ko Loh Li (戈登路), Av. Edward VII, French Concession.
My cousin is the proprietor of the Chung Mei Printing Company
(中美) at that address.    About two weeks ago a friend
of mine named Wong Ying (王英) introduced me to one named
Zung (宗) who I understand is a teacher.    Zung told me
that he would try to find a position as teacher for me. I
visited Zung at his house No.1338, Lane 945, Haining Road,
three or four times.    I did not meet anybody at his house
until the evening of 12/1/34 when I found him in company with
another man.    It was about 6 p.m.    Shortly afterwards two
more men arrived.    I never saw any of these three men before
and do not know their names.    Zung and I talked about the
possibility of getting a position for me. At about 7 p.m. Zung
went out to order some food for us and while he was absent
the Police came and we were all arrested.

I do not know the reason of my arrest. I do not
belong to the Communist or any other political party. I know
nothing about the books and pamphlets seized by the Police in
the room.    I think they belong to Zung.

(Signed) Koh Ying.
tasks.zh:

南京                                副督察 普罗科菲耶夫 (S.S.I. Prokofiev)
西虹口巡捕房        1934年1月13日                  书记员 方国田 (Fang Kuo Tien)

我叫郭英，21岁，南京人，无业。我最初从南京来到上海，在南京的一所中学读书直到1932年夏天，之后我与父母住在那里。此后我一直与我的表亲郭淼（Koh Miao）住在法租界爱多亚路戈登路（Ko Loh Li）63号。我的表亲是该地址中美印刷公司（Chung Mei Printing Company）的老板。大约两周前，我的一位名叫王英（Wong Ying）的朋友将我介绍给一位名叫宗（Zung）的人，据我了解他是一名教师。宗告诉我，他会尽力为我找一个教师的职位。我曾去过三次或四次他在海宁路945弄1338号的住所。在他家里我没有遇到任何人，直到1934年1月12日晚上，我发现他和另一个男人在一起。大约是下午6点。不久之后，又有两个男人到达。我以前从未见过这三个人，也不知道他们的名字。宗和我谈论了为我谋取职位的可能性。大约晚上7点，宗出去为我们订购食物，当他不在时，警察来了，我们都被捕了。

我不知道我被捕的原因。我不属于共产党或任何其他政党。我对警察在房间里查获的书籍和小册子一无所知。我想它们属于宗。

（签名）郭英。

Central Notification No.202

The day (February 7) on which the Soviet General
Conference will be held is fast approaching, yet up
to the present very little has been achieved concerning
the election of representatives to attend the Conference
as well as the despatch of these representatives. More-
over it is noticed that not all the representatives are
being selected from the people.

It is the paramount duty of the Party to urge the
people to struggle for the success of the Soviet Political
Power and the establishment of a Soviet Central Government,
especially at present when the Imperialists and the
Kuomintang are endeavouring to annihilate the Red Army,
and conquer the Soviet Districts by force of arms, while
the Trotsky Clique is employing slogans opposing the
1st National Soviet General Conference with the object
of deceiving the people. The Party should mobilize all
its forces to oppose the attack upon the Soviet Districts
by the Imperialists and the Kuomintang, and at the
same time complete arrangements should be made for the
election of representatives from the proletariat to attend
the Conference.

All Party branches should, especially when the
Kuomintang is using slogans in support of the National
People's Convention to attack the Soviet, point out to
the people that according to the election regulations
of this deceitful Convention, only representatives of
landlords, capitalists and traitors belonging to "Yellow"
Labour or Peasants' Unions are permitted to participate
and furthermore this Convention will not interest itself
in the welfare of the proletariat. Also explain to
them that only through the Soviet Political Power can the
proletariat obtain relief and that the Soviet election
takes place only among the real populace. During this
propaganda campaign, efforts must be made to seize the
first opportunity to carry out the election of representatives
from among the real populace for participation in the
Soviet General Conference.

In conclusion, the various Party branches should
expedite the election of representatives and for their
despatch, at the same time intensifying the propaganda
opposing the National People's Convention and the
attack on the Soviet Districts by the Kuomintang and the
Imperialists. Representatives selected must be
despatched according to the instructions laid down by the
Central Preparatory Committee.

The Central.

'Workers' Correspondence Issue No. 1' bearing on the
financial status of the Nanking Government.

Shanghai, Jan. 20.

In view of the economic crisis together with the prolonged
period of civil war among the militarists, the financial status
of the Nanking militaristic Government has almost reached
complete bankruptcy. In order to prolong its existence,
it has depended upon loans and debenture bonds. On
top of these, still more loans are being made by various
provinces which are already in bankrupt states.

Further, the Nanking Government has increased the
customs revenues from January 1 this year and abolished
likin in order to relieve its financial embarrassment and
to attack communistic movements. It has also proposed
to convene a citizens' conference on May 5 to deceive the
people.

The treacherous Nanking Government first secured the approval
of the imperialists to increase customs revenues and granted them certain great
privileges in exchange. In November last year the Nanking
Government invited representatives of the various foreign powers to
Nanking to discuss the readjustment of domestic and foreign
loans. At that conference it was proposed to raise a
huge loan to be known as the 'Reorganization Loan' with the
new customs surtax as security. According to a report
which appeared in the Shanghai Tung Shin Pao (Jan. 18),
in December last year, the total amount of foreign loans
made to China is $1,700,000,000. Foreign loans have
more or less contributed to the civil wars among the militarists
in China.

The abolition of likin is equivalent to an increase
in customs revenues.

In November last year the Nanking Government promulgated
a law authorizing the levying of a special tax, a business
tax and a tax on goods leaving factories. These taxes are
intended to replace the losses which will be incurred after
the abolition of likin. The present Nanking officials
have deprived the people of all their interests by means of
these taxes.

Although the Nanking Government has issued debenture bonds,
increased customs revenues and imposed higher rates of taxes,
it is still unable to solve its financial difficulties. The
proposal to float a large foreign loan affords an excellent
opportunity to the imperialists to seize China. The American
imperialists propose to lend 100,000 ounces of silver to the

《工人通讯》第一期，涉及南京政府的财政状况。

上海，1月20日。

鉴于经济危机以及军阀之间长期的内战，南京军阀政府的财政状况几乎已陷入完全破产。为了延续其存在，它一直依赖贷款和公债债券。除此之外，各个已经处于破产状态的省份还在举借更多的贷款。

此外，南京政府从今年1月1日起增加了关税收入并废除了厘金，以缓解其财政困境并打击共产主义运动。它还提议于5月5日召开国民会议以欺骗人民。

卖国的南京政府首先获得了帝国主义者对增加关税收入的批准，并以此交换给予他们某些重大特权。去年11月，南京政府邀请各外国列强代表前往南京，讨论调整内外债问题。在那次会议上，提议以新的关税附加税为担保，筹集一笔巨额贷款，称为“整理借款”。据《上海通社报》（1月18日）刊登的一篇报道，去年12月，外国对华贷款总额为1,700,000,000美元。外国贷款在某种程度上助长了中国军阀之间的内战。

废除厘金等同于增加关税收入。

去年11月，南京政府颁布了一项法律，授权征收特别税、营业税和出厂货物税。这些税收旨在弥补废除厘金后造成的损失。现任南京官员通过这些税收剥夺了人民的所有利益。

尽管南京政府发行了公债债券，增加了关税收入并提高了税率，但仍无法解决其财政困难。提出发行大规模外债的建议，为帝国主义者攫取中国提供了绝佳机会。美国帝国主义者提议向中国军阀提供10万盎司白银。英国和加拿大政府也打算向南京政府提供大额贷款。上海的英国帝国主义报纸报道称，南京政府希望以关税收入、铁路利润和盐税为担保，筹集一笔大规模的整理借款。这笔贷款的一部分将指定用于调整内外债，其余部分将用于整编南京军队以攻击共产主义运动。提议所有内外债将在三十年内还清。

tasks.title: Fuhtan University & Middle School
tasks.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, March 27, 1936

Trouble At Fuh Tan
FIRST-HAND investigation of the trouble at
Fuh Tan university, Klangwan, discloses
background reasons for anxiety and possible
action by the constituted authorities but fails
to give the police a clear bill of health in the
matter of discretion.
It is always difficult to piece together a
completely coherent account of such affairs.
As we have obtained the story from both
school and municipal sources it seems agreed
that there was a police raid Tuesday night
which was successful insofar as it affected
dormitories outside the university but un-
successful within the institution where an
alarm was raised and resistance made; that
the police put a cordon about and became
involved in a serious fight Tuesday afternoon
culminating in the firing of shots which
wounded two policemen through the legs; and
that search of the university was made yester-
day morning. In this last the school authori-
ties co-operated but they seem to have been
participants and sufferers in the previous
trouble.
Upon details there is a wide variety of
disagreement with much of this naturally
centering around the question of responsibility.
On the showing of the City Government there
was reason to fear trouble in the university
with a clash between conflicting factions. The
underlying situation has been compared with
that at Chinan university, Chenju, a few
months ago when police conducted a search
just before pitched battle is said to have been
scheduled between contending groups with the
result that half a truckload of sticks and other
crude weapons together with more deadly
shotguns and pistols is stated to have been
seized.
In the case of Fuh Tan, the authorities
are said to have had information that due in
large part to the unsupervised condition of
outside dormitories, many trouble-makers not
even connected with the university were
taking a leading part in fomenting disorders
under the shield of a number of pseudo-
literary and other societies. A list of names,
apparently including seven in outside dormi-
tories and one or two inside the grounds, had
been prepared—on information which seems
to have been compiled by a particularly
assiduous spy system maintained by the police
—and the authorities decided to swoop down
on the eve of a great mass-meeting in con-
nection with organization work for the
National Salvation Association. The clear im-
plication is that the raids were conducted in
a desire to avert possible serious disorders
within the institution; i.e. a purging of Fuh
Tan for Fuh Tan's good.
Evidently there were plenty among the
students who did not look at the matter in
that light, judging from the warm reception
accorded the searching party of Tuesday night.
It seems impossible to get any very accurate
story on how the Wednesday afternoon affair
arose, but apparently when a serious situation
develops it is the practice of the police to set
plain-clothes and uniformed men at various
strategic points within the university, and it
would appear that under such circumstances
it would not be difficult to set fire to such
matters.
We are informed by the City Government
that the police about the main gate, who be-
came the center of a protracted battle waged
upon the campus (perhaps drawn in by dif-
ficulties encountered by their comrades station-
ed inside, though there is also a version that
they thought the gate was being stormed)
were armed only with bamboo staves and that
such men as had guns were kept at a distance.
We are inclined to give the authorities credit
for having handled this in the manner
described although it is hard to understand
why the situation was allowed to develop as
it did in the hours after the searching-party's
visit. Apparently the Wednesday afternoon
battle went on for a long time, perhaps a
couple of hours, and it was finally halted by
the sound of the shots—which school sources
say came from outside the grounds though the
police have a different view, and were the suf-
ferers.
The police search of Wednesday morning
occurred more than a day after the first hunt
for student "communists", or whatever they
are to be called, and that it was not par-
ticularly fruitful is hardly to be wondered at;
even had the university been a virtual arsenal
last Tuesday, by Thursday morning there was
ample time to dispose of the contraband.
We note that the China Press waxes sar-
castic over our publication of a letter from a
student eye-witness, "presuming" that he did
not use a nom de plume and indicating that
upon this point hinges the whole value of the
letter. Certainly a nom de plume was used.
We have no desire to jeopardize a student's
personal safety for nothing worse than an
honest effort at reporting, which may have
erred in detail but in the main gave a sound
and colorful picture. The China Press itself
in the same editorial, remarks that "unfor-
tunately, when the incident happened, Mayor
Wu Te-chen was in Nanking" whereas the
search was made Tuesday night when the first
clash occurred, the main battle occurred
Wednesday afternoon, and it was not until
Wednesday night that Mayor Wu left for Nan-
king. This merely to illustrate humanity's
common proneness to error!
To sum up, the police seem to us to be
operating on rather dubious ground when they
subsidize spies within the universities and
proceed on a basis of evidence thus gathered
rather than cooperation with the school
authorities, and in this specific incident they
appear to have erred by alternate plungings
and hesitations.
Even a brief visit at Fuh Tan shows belief
among the students that their ranks are
honeycombed by "G-men", students and others
paid to be informers concerning various
brands of radicalism. This makes for a gen-
erally unwholesome situation, and information
gathered by such means is likely to be tainted
by agent provocateur flavor. If, however, the
police deem it best to operate by such means,

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年3月27日，星期五

复旦发生骚乱

对江湾复旦大学骚乱的第一手调查，揭示了当局感到焦虑并可能采取行动的背景原因，但在警方的审慎行事方面，却未能给予其清白的证明。

要将此类事件拼凑成一个完全连贯的叙述总是困难的。既然我们从学校和市政两方面获得了消息，似乎各方都同意以下事实：周二晚上警方进行了一次突袭，就影响大学校外宿舍而言是成功的，但在校内则未成功，因为校内发出了警报并进行了抵抗；周二下午，警方包围了学校并卷入了一场严重的斗殴，最终以开枪告终，导致两名警察腿部中弹受伤；昨天上午对大学进行了搜查。在最后一次行动中，校方予以配合，但他们似乎是此前骚乱的参与者和受害者。

在细节上存在广泛的分歧，其中许多自然集中在责任问题上。根据市政府的说法，有理由担心大学内因派系冲突而发生麻烦。潜在局势被比作几个月前陈居（Chenju，音译）暨南大学的情况，当时警方据称在各对立团体预定展开激战前夕进行了搜查，结果查获了半卡车的棍棒和其他粗制武器，以及更为致命的猎枪和手枪。

据称，在复旦一案中，当局掌握的情报显示，由于校外宿舍缺乏监管，许多甚至与大学无关的捣乱分子，在一些伪文学社团及其他社团的掩护下，在煽动混乱方面起着主导作用。一份名单已经拟定——该名单似乎是由警方维持的一个特别勤勉的间谍系统所汇编的情报为基础——名单上显然包括七名校外宿舍人员和一两名校内人员，当局决定在一次与救国会组织工作有关的大型群众集会前夕采取突击行动。其明确含义是，进行突袭是为了避免校内可能发生严重混乱；即为了复旦的利益而对复旦进行清洗。

显然，学生中有很多人并不这样看待此事，从周二晚上搜查队受到的“热烈”接待即可判断。似乎无法获得关于周三下午事件如何发生的非常准确的说法，但显然，当局势变得严重时，警方的做法是在校内各个战略要点部署便衣和制服警察，在这种情况下，点燃此类事端似乎并不难。

我们从市政府获悉，驻守在大门口的警察成为了在校园内进行的持久战斗的中心（也许是被驻守在内部的同事所遇到的困难所吸引，尽管也有一种说法认为他们以为大门正遭到冲击），他们只配备了竹棍，而持有枪支的人员则被保持在远处。我们倾向于相信当局是以所述方式处理此事的，尽管很难理解为何在搜查队造访后的几个小时内，局势会发展成那样。显然，周三下午的战斗持续了很长时间，也许有两个小时，最终因枪声而停止——校方消息来源称枪声来自校外，尽管警方持有不同观点，并且是受害者。

周三上午的警方搜查发生在第一次搜捕学生“共产主义者”（或无论怎么称呼他们）的一天多之后，其成果并不特别丰硕，这也不足为奇；即使上周二大学里实际上是个军火库，到周四早上也有充足的时间来处理违禁品。

我们注意到，《字林西报》对我们刊登的一封学生目击者的来信极尽讽刺之能事，“推测”他并未使用笔名，并指出整封信的价值都取决于这一点。当然，使用了笔名。我们无意仅仅因为一次诚实的报道努力而危及学生的人身安全，该报道可能在细节上有误，但总体上提供了可靠且生动的画面。《字林西报》在同一篇社论中指出，“不幸的是，当事件发生时，吴铁城市长正在南京”，而搜查是在周二晚上首次冲突发生时进行的，主要战斗发生在周三下午，直到周三晚上吴市长才前往南京。这只是为了说明人类普遍容易犯错的倾向！

总之，在我们看来，当警方在大学内部资助间谍，并以此类收集到的证据而非与校方合作为基础采取行动时，他们的立场是相当可疑的，而在这一特定事件中，他们似乎因交替出现的鲁莽冲动和犹豫不决而犯了错误。

即使在复旦短暂停留也能看出，学生们相信他们的队伍中布满了“G-men”（政府特工），即学生和受雇报告各种激进主义情况的其他人。这造成了一种普遍不健康的局面，通过此类手段收集的信息很可能带有挑衅代理人（agent provocateur）的色彩。然而，如果警方认为最好以这种方式行动，

tasks.en:

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of C.P.C. 1644 Nyung Ching Kwei ( )
native of....................................................taken by me Self.
at Louza Station on the 28-11-38 and interpreted by translated Clerk Pang Wei Hsin.

I was detailed for traffic duty on Chekiang Road and
Avenue Edward VII corner between 12 noon and 4 p.m. on
28-11-38.

At 3.55 p.m. on 28-11-38 I heard the reports of gun-shot
about 4 or 5 times behind me on Chekiang Road and at the same
instant a Route 5 Tramcar was proceeding from North to South
on Chekiang Road coming towards me and the sounds of gun-shot
arose from the rear of this tramcar.

As soon as I heard the reports of gun-shot, I took out
my own pistol, I loaded it and I ran to the place about 70 to
80 yards away from my post.

Only a few steps I ran from my post but I heard no more
reports of gun-shot .

Upon arrival at the scene all pedestrians have scattered
and I only saw the murdered man lying on the ground and I asked
him by whom he was killed but he gave no answer. Apparently he
was dead.

I asked different shops in the near vicinity if they saw
the murderers or into what direction they escaped but they
denied seeing anything. When I looked around but I did not
see any suspects.

I hastened back to my post and I reported the facts to
Station over telephone.

Signed: C.P.C. 1644 Nyung Ching Kwei

以下是华人巡长1644号熊景贵（ ）的陈述，籍贯....................................................，由我本人于1938年11月28日在老闸捕房录取，由翻译书记员庞维新口译。

1938年11月28日中午12点至下午4点之间，我被派往浙江路与爱多亚路转角处执行交通勤务。

1938年11月28日下午3点55分，我听到身后浙江路传来约4或5声枪响，与此同时，一辆5路电车正沿浙江路从北向南朝我驶来，枪声是从这辆电车后方传来的。

一听到枪声，我拔出自己的手枪，装上子弹，跑向离我岗位约70至80码的地方。

我刚离开岗位跑了几步，就再也听不到枪声了。

到达现场时，所有行人均已散开，我只看到被杀者躺在地上，我问他被谁所杀，但他没有回答。显然他已经死亡。

我问附近各家商店是否看到凶手或他们逃往哪个方向，但他们否认看到任何情况。我环顾四周，但没有看到任何嫌疑人。

我急忙回到岗位，并通过电话向捕房报告了事实。

签名：华人巡长 1644号 熊景贵

Mei Feng Silk Weaving Factory - ex-workers agitate for
reopening of the concern

Some 300 ex-workers of the Mei Feng Silk Weaving
Factory ly Haichow Road, are agitating for the reopining
of the concern which in consequence of trade depression
closed down on December 31, 1933 (Vide I.R. 1-3/1/34).
During the afternoon of January 1, some 120 ex-employees
held a meeting on the premises of the factory, when it was
decided that four delegates be assigned to negotiate with
the management regarding resumption of operations. It was
also resolved that all affected workers should contribute
$3.00 each to cover expenses incurred by the delegates.
It is learned that the ex-workers propose to hold a meeting
this morning, January 4, on the premises of the concern to
discuss ways and means of soliciting assistance from the
Chinese Authorities.

TSEU TAO FENG & THE CHUNG HWA VOCATIONAL INSTITUTE

The money to pay for the expenses of the Chung Hwa Vocational Institute (中華職業教育社) is contributed by various parties, including the Kiangsu Provincial Government which issues a monthly allowance of $2,000 out of its educational funds.
Believing that Tseu Tao Feng (鄒韜奮 publisher and editor of the defunct "Mass Livelihood" Weekly Magazine 大眾生活 ) was attached to the institute and that the periodical published by Tseu was also connected with it, the Kiangsu Provincial Government recently cancelled the monthly allowance. Tseu Tao Feng was at one time connected with the institute, but he later severed his connection.
Through the efforts of Woo Shih Huei (吳稚暉), member of the Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang, and Nyu Yung Chien (鈕永建), Chief of the Educational Funds Control Office of Kiangsu Province, the monthly allowance is again being issued to the institute.

Eastern Times and other local newspapers:

TROUBLE AT FUTAN UNIVERSITY

Upon receipt of information that a number of communists, who are students of Futan University, are planning to create disturbances, the Garrison Commissioner of Woosung and Shanghai on the evening of March 24 ordered the Bureau of Public Safety to detail officers to the University to make a raid. The Police arrested six students named Wong Pah San (黃拔山), Mao Tsze Shing (莫自新), Pao Nee (包毅), Chiang Veng Cheng (蔣文蒸), Chen Tung Che (陳通徹) and Kiang Nan Tsong (江南俊) and at noon of March 25 they arrested another student named Yang Pah Pang (楊伯鵬).
Certain communist elements in the University then instigated the students to organize a guard over the front and rear gates of the University and to prohibit anybody leaving or entering. During the trouble about 20 shots were fired. Lee Bai Woo (李伯武) of the Bureau of Public Safety and two policemen were injured.
With a view to maintaining peace, the Garrison Commissioner has instructed the authorities of Futan University to hand over the students who had opened fire and to warn the students not to be utilized by communists.

My name is Koo Ah Shing, agr 17, native of Pootung,
unemployed printer. From the age of 6 to 10 years I studied
at a private school in my native place, after which I assisted
my father in farming work. At the age of 13 I started to work
as an apprentice at a printing establishment in Pootung. I
then came to Shanghai and worked at the Commercial Press for
about 3 months when I was dismissed owing to the reduction of
staff. I returned to my native place and have since been
working on my father's farm. On January 7, 1934, I came to
Shanghai from my native place in order to find some employment
here. I lived in various small lodging houses situated in
the vicinity of the Great World, French Concession. I do
not know the location of the lodging houses. At about 6 p.m.
12-1-34 I went to No.1538 lane 945, Haining Road, to visit my
friend named Zung (曾) who is a teacher at some school in
Shanghai. I met Zung about 8 years when I was employed at
the Commercial Press. Zung promised me to find work. Apart
from Zung there were one female and two males in the room. I
never saw these people before and I do not know their names.
Zung and I had a talk about the possibility of finding a job
for me. He then went out saying he would get some food for us.
while he was absent the Police arrived and arrested all those
present in the room.

I know nothing about the books and pamphlets seized by
the Police in the room. I think they belong to Zung. He never
gave me any book to read. I am not a communist and do not
belong to any political party.

(Signed) Koo Ah Shing.

March 27, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE TROUBLE AT FUTAN UNIVERSITY

Newspapers published reports yesterday to the effect that certain communist elements were in hiding in Futan University, that seven students had been arrested by the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters and that the communists opened fire and wounded several policemen of the Bureau of Public Safety.

Before his departure for Nanking on the night of March 25, Mayor Wu Teh Chen ordered that another search be made for the reactionary elements who had opened fire. Lai Tseng (賴 棻), Director of the General Affairs Department of the Ministry of Education, who had been directed by the Ministry to assist the Shanghai City Government, arrived in Shanghai yesterday morning.

At 6 a.m. yesterday, the Peace Preservation Corps and the Bureau of Public Safety carried out another search within the university in conjunction with Chien Sing Tse (錢 新 之), Chairman of the Board of Directors of the university, Li Tung Huei (李 登 輝), the Principal, and King Tung Ying (金 通 尹), the Chief Secretary of the university. The search lasted about one hour after which the university authorities requested Lai Tseng, Director of the General Affairs Department of the Ministry of Education, O.K. Yui, Chief Secretary of the Shanghai City Government, and Pan Kung Tsai, Commissioner of the Bureau of Education, to withdraw the officers of the Peace Preservation Corps and the Bureau of Public Safety. The university authorities have also promised to comply with the following demands:-
(1) That the university authorities surrender the students who had opened fire.
(2) That the university authorities conduct a voluntary search for the communist elements who are still at large and surrender them to the authorities.
(3) That the national salvation association formed by the reactionary elements be dissolved.
(4) That normal conditions and studies be resumed after the withdrawal of the members of the Peace Preservation Corps and the Police.
(5) That the university authorities accept responsibility for the recovery of two rifles and more than 300 bayonets which were used for the military training of the students and which have disappeared from the armoury.
(6) That the university authorities extend protection to those students who are regarded as traitors by the communists because of their opposition.

The officers of the Police and the Peace Preservation Corps were withdrawn from the university premises yesterday afternoon. It is learned that a policeman named Hou Sung Tseng (侯 松 增), who was wounded, succumbed to his injuries at the Red Cross Hospital at 3 p.m. yesterday.

Sin Wan Pao (Evening Edition) published the following telegram from Nanking:-

Mayor Wu Teh Chen arrived here yesterday morning and called upon Wang Shih Chih, Minister of Education, and General Chang Chun, Minister of Foreign Affairs and discussed with them measures to deal with the trouble at the Futan University.

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

复旦大学事件

各报昨日刊登消息称，某些共产党分子藏匿于复旦大学，七名学生已被吴淞上海警备司令部逮捕，且共产党分子开枪击伤数名公安局警察。

吴铁城市长在3月25日晚启程前往南京之前，下令再次搜捕开枪的反动分子。受教育部指派协助上海市政府的教育部总务司司长赖棻（Lai Tseng）于昨晨抵达上海。

昨晨6时，保安队与公安局在该校董事会主席钱新之（Chien Sing Tse）、校长李登辉（Li Tung Huei）及大学主任秘书金通尹（King Tung Ying）的陪同下，在校内再次进行搜查。搜查持续约一小时，随后校方要求教育部总务司司长赖棻、上海市政府秘书长俞鸿钧（O.K. Yui，音译）及教育局局长潘公展（Pan Kung Tsai，音译）撤走保安队及公安局人员。校方亦承诺履行以下要求：
(1) 校方交出开枪的学生。
(2) 校方主动搜捕仍在逃的共产党分子并将其移交当局。
(3) 解散由反动分子组织的救国会。
(4) 在保安队及警察撤离后，恢复常态及教学秩序。

(6) 校方保护那些因反对共产党而被其视为汉奸的学生。

警察及保安队人员于昨日下午从校园撤离。据悉，一名名叫侯松增（Hou Sung Tseng）的受伤警察于昨日下午3时在红十字会医院因伤重不治身亡。

吴铁城市长于昨晨抵达此地，拜会了教育部长王世杰及外交部长张群将军，并与他们商讨了处理复旦大学事件的措施。

tasks.title: Assassination Of A Reformed Government Official Chu Koh Ping
tasks.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
NOV 29 1938
Another Murder in
Troubled Louza
Political Motive Seen in
Avenue Edward Shooting;
Desperadoes Escape

Yet another murder of a Chinese
took place in the Louza district
yesterday afternoon when unidenti-
fied desperados riddled their victim
with pistol bullets at the crowded
intersection of Chekiang Road and
Avenue Edward VII, and escaped.
The target for the assassins' fusillade
who died almost instantly, was Chu
Koh-ping, 42, a native of Changchow
who was formerly an employee of the
Garrison Commander's office of the
new "regime." No-one else was
wounded.

The bold attack occurred at exactly
3.55 o'clock. Apparently the gunmen
waylaid their victim, who was on
foot, and sprayed him with bullets
at close range. His head and body
had six wounds, attesting six direct
hits, when examined later at the
Lester Chinese Hospital, where he
was taken in a Fire Brigade am-
bulance. Two automatic pistols were
used, one being of .38 calibre and
the other a .32.

Possibly more than six shots were
fired by the murderers, but only the
half dozen took effect in the victim's
body. The rain of bullets naturally
caused a panic among pedestrians
and others at the populous crossing
and made scores of persons scamper
into alleyways and shops in search
of safety. It was considered remark-
able that no-one else was hit by the
fusillade.

Political Motive?

The body was taken to the Public
Mortuary last night. The man was
of the "loafer" type, to which the
Chinese terms "pi-san" or "liu-mang"
are applied. The murder was sus-
pected to be of political nature, and
hence detectives of the S.M.P. Head-
quarters special homicide office were
called in to assist Louza Station in
the investigation.

As a result of yesterday's assassina-
tion and two previous ones, all of
which took place in the same dis-
trict inside four days, the police
redoubled their efforts last night to
comb the Louza lodging-house
neighbourhoods and alleyways for
suspicious characters. Search-parties
operated at regular intervals and
many suspects were challenged both
on the street and in houses. Head-
quarters detectives also made a
number of raids through the day
and evening.

Other Victim Identified

His fingerprints yesterday identified
the Chinese who was shot in a Can-
ton Road lodging-house on Sunday
night. The man was wounded in the
head at 9 p.m. that evening while
in room 40 of the Pao Woo Lodging
House, Lane 420, Canton Road. He
died in the Lester Chinese Hospital
about two hours later. Only one
bullet was fired, from a .32 calibre
automatic pistol.

The victim was subsequently
identified by fingerprint experts who
found that he possessed a criminal
record in Shanghai, having been
handed over to the Chinese authori-
ties here by the Settlement Police in
1932 to answer to a charge.

His murderer escaped from the
Canton Road lodging-house and has
not been identified. The motive for
the killing was probably political
also in this case.

《字林西报》，
1938年11月29日
老闸区动荡中再发命案
爱多亚路枪击案疑有政治动机；暴徒逃脱

昨天下午，老闸区又发生了一起中国人被杀案件， unidentified desperados（身份不明的暴徒）在浙江路与爱多亚路拥挤的十字路口用手枪子弹将受害者打得千疮百孔，随后逃脱。刺客齐射的目标是朱国平（Chu Koh-ping），42岁，常州人，曾是新“政权”卫戍司令部的雇员，他几乎当场死亡。没有其他人受伤。

这起大胆的攻击恰好发生在3点55分。显然，枪手伏击了步行的受害者，并在近距离向他扫射。后来在莱斯德华医院（Lester Chinese Hospital）进行检查时，发现他的头部和身体有六处伤口，证实有六次直接命中，他是被消防队救护车送往该医院的。凶手使用了两支自动手枪，一支为.38口径，另一支为.32口径。

凶手可能发射了超过六发子弹，但只有这六发击中了受害者的身体。弹雨自然在人口稠密的十字路口引起了行人和其他人的恐慌，使得数十人逃入小巷和商店寻求安全。值得注意的是，齐射中没有其他人被击中。

政治动机？

尸体昨晚被送往公共停尸房。此人属于“无业游民”类型，中文称为“皮三”或“流氓”。谋杀案被怀疑具有政治性质，因此工部局警务处总部特别凶杀股的侦探被召来协助老闸捕房进行调查。

由于昨天的刺杀案以及此前两天内发生在同一地区的另外两起案件，警方昨晚加倍努力，搜查老闸区的旅馆街区和小巷，寻找可疑人物。搜查队定期行动，许多嫌疑人在街道上和房屋内受到盘查。总部侦探也在白天和晚上进行了多次突袭。

另一名受害者身份确认

通过指纹，昨天确认了周日晚上在广东路一家旅馆被枪杀的中国人的身份。当晚9点，该男子在广东路420弄宝武旅馆40号房间内头部中弹。约两小时后，他在莱斯德华医院死亡。只发射了一发子弹，来自一支.32口径的自动手枪。

随后，指纹专家确认了受害者的身份，发现他在上海有犯罪记录，曾于1932年被租界警察移交给此处中国当局以应对指控。

他的凶手从广东路旅馆逃脱，身份尚未确认。在此案中，杀人动机可能也是政治性的。

Made by D. S. Craig Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
Further enquiries were made at the Mei Foong (美丰)
Silk Filature, 83 Haichow Road by C. D. C. 108 A. M. 17/5/39
when it was ascertained that at 4 p.m. 16/5/39, two
workers named Woo Ah Loong (吴阿龙) and Zung Ah Tsaung
(张阿昌) representing the strikers, had met the
proprietor Lee Loong Siau (李隆萧) in the offices of
the Mei Foong Silk Filature and discussed the possibi-
lity of commencing work at the increase per yard as
demanded. The proprietor agreed to give an increase
of one half cent per yard but this was refused by the
representatives who stated they would accept one cent
increase per yard and start work immediately but this
was refused by the proprietor. The 46 workers are still
on strike although there are 20 female and 8 male
employees still at work. No threats of intimidation or
other untoward incident has occurred.
